## AURELIAN, Archbishop XXIII

Aurelian XXIII, a distinguished man, young in age but mature in judgment and surpassingly elegant in every grace, died in peace after a few years, on the eighth [seventh] day before the Kalends of June. He was buried in the church of the Apostles beside the ambo, at the place where blessed Neon rests.

## ECCLESIUS, Archbishop XXIV

Ecclesius XXIV. According to various accounts, he was the builder of the church of Saint Mary Major; in his time the church of the martyr Saint Vitalis was built by Julian the banker. No church in Italy is like it. Twenty-six thousand gold solidi were spent on it. He occupied the see for 3 years, 6 months, and 8 days. He lies in the church of Saint Vitalis. He died at the age of 62 [in the year 562].

## URSICINUS, Archbishop XXV

[Col. 0783C]

Ursicinus XXV, a humble man. In his time the church of Saint Apollinaris was built by Julian the banker. No church resembles it, because at night it shines almost as brightly as in the day. He was buried in the basilica of blessed Vitalis [the martyr], before the altar of Saint Nazarius. He occupied the see for 3 years, 6 months, and 8 days.

## VICTOR, Archbishop XXVI

Victor XXVI, handsome in face and cheerful in countenance. Builder of Tricolis, but not its completer. He also made a silver *ciborium* over the altar of the holy Ursian church, and for this purpose distributed the revenues of all Italy; it is written that these amounted to 120 pounds of silver by true weight. [Note: [Col. 0783D] By a later hand. BACCH.] He died on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of May [March], around the year of the Lord 568 [568]. He was buried [Col. 0783D] in the aforementioned church of Saint Vitalis, beneath the monastery of Saint Nazarius. He occupied the see for 6 years, 11 months, and 11 days.

## MAXIMIAN, Archbishop XXVII

Maximian XXVII, tall [long-lived] in stature, bald of head. Builder of many churches, which it would take too long to recount. He consecrated the church of Classis. He died on the eighth day before the Kalends of May [March]. He rests in the monastery of Saint Andrew the Apostle.

## AGNELLUS, Archbishop XXVIII

[Col. 0784B]

Agnellus XXVIII, ruddy in face. This archbishop himself acquired silver for the church of Ravenna. He built the monastery of Saint George there. In his time the Franks were expelled from Italy, and Justinian Augustus died at Constantinople. [Note: [Col. 0783D] By a later hand. ID.] He died on the day before the Kalends of August, in the year 566 [566]. He occupied the see for 13 years, 1 month, and 8 days. The aforementioned Agnellus was buried in the church of Saint Agatha Major, and [in the church] of the [other] martyr.

## PETRUS THE ELDER, Archbishop XXIX

Petrus the Elder XXIX, advanced in age, was mature both in judgment and in body. He founded the church of blessed Severus the Confessor, but did not complete it, around the year of the Lord 578 [578]. At that time Venetia was occupied by the Lombards, and they were expelled without a battle. [Col. 0784C] [Note: [Col. 0783D] By a later hand. ID.] He died on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of September. He was buried in the city of Classis, in a large stone sarcophagus, in the church of Saint Probus. He occupied the see for 8 years, 2 months, and 18 days.

## JOHN THE ROMAN, Archbishop XXX

John [II the Roman] XXX, completer and consecrator of the church of Saint Severus. He occupied the see for 16 years, [lacuna] months, and 18 days.

## MAURITIUS, Archbishop XXXI

Mauritius XXXI, [Note: [Col. 0783D] By a later hand. ID.] also called Marinianus. He was Roman by birth, very handsome in every respect. He was the nephew of the aforementioned John, his predecessor. In his time a terrifying sign appeared in the sky, and Theodoric, king of the Franks, waged war with his paternal cousin Lothar. [Note: [Col. 0783D] By a later hand. ID.] He died on the tenth day before the Kalends of November. He was buried in the *ardica* [read: *ardica*] of blessed Apollinaris outside the walls [Col. 0784D] of Classis, which had been consecrated by blessed Pope Gregory around the year 597 [599].

## JOHN, Archbishop XXXII

John of Classis XXXII. [Note: [Col. 0784D] By a later hand. ID.] John III. He was full-bodied, handsome in appearance [handsome], and a follower of every good thing. He was buried in the *ardica* of blessed Apollinaris. [Note: [Col. 0784D] By a later hand. ID.] He held the see in the year of the Lord 605, in the time of the emperor Phocas. [Note: [Col. 0784D] Marginal note: “He occupied the see for 5 years, 10 months, and 18 days.” John of Classis flourished around the year of the Lord 606.]

## JOHN, Archbishop XXXIII

[Col. 0785A]

John IV, XXXIII. He was buried in the *ardica* of blessed Apollinaris. He lived in the time of Pope Boniface; until his time and the time of the emperor Phocas, the Church of Constantinople had been first-ranking. [Note: [Col. 0785D] I noted in its proper place that this was impiously and falsely written by Agnellus. ID.—By a later hand. ID.] At that time the years of the Lord were 693 [600]. He occupied the see for 18 years, 6 months, and 8 days.

## BONUS, Archbishop XXXIV

Bonus XXXIV. He was Bonus in name and in deeds. [Note: [Col. 0785D] By a later hand. ID.] He died on the seventh day before the Kalends of September. He was buried in the basilica of blessed Apollinaris the martyr at Classis.

## MAURUS, Archbishop XXXV

Maurus XXXV, who excommunicated the pope. [Note: [Col. 0785D] These schismatic statements were copied from Agnellus. ID.] In the time of the emperor Constantine, he freed his Church from the yoke of Roman servitude. [Col. 0785B] [Note: [Col. 0785D] By a later hand. ID.] Maurus lived around the year of the Lord 668 [668]. He occupied the see for 28 years, 10 months, and 18 days. He was buried in the *aidica* of blessed Apollinaris.

## REPARATUS, Archbishop XXXVI

Reparatus XXXVI. Advanced in age. [Note: [Col. 0785D] This is from Agnellus. ID.] He did not subject himself to the Roman see. He relieved priests in their poverty. He therefore died on the third day before the Kalends of August and was buried in the church of blessed Apollinaris. He occupied the see for 5 years and 8 months.

## THEODORUS, Archbishop XXXVII

Theodorus XXXVII. [Note: [Col. 0785D] These are Agnellus’s words. ID.] Young in age, terrifying in appearance, dreadful to behold, and full of every deceit. This most ferocious man died with great rejoicing among the priests [Col. 0785C] on 18 January. He was buried in the *ardica* of blessed Apollinaris. He occupied the see for 13 years, 3 months, and 20 days.

## DAMIANUS, Archbishop XXXVIII

Damianus XXXVIII. He raised a dead man. He died on the third day before the Ides of May. He was buried in the church of blessed Apollinaris. He occupied the see for 16 years, 2 months, and 16 days.

## FELIX, Archbishop XXXIX

Felix XXXIX. He was a well-watered spring, an excellent father, an outstanding preacher, and the author of many volumes. [Note: [Col. 0785D] By a later hand. ID.] He died on 25 November, around the year of the Lord 793 [700]. He was buried in the church of blessed Apollinaris. He occupied the see for 16 years, 7 months, and 24 days.

## JOHN, Archbishop XL

[Col. 0785D]

John, [Note: [Col. 0785D] By a later hand. ID.] the fifth, XL. He was exceedingly wise, humble, and gentle. In his time the Petriana church collapsed in an earthquake around the year of the Lord 901 [801], after the solemn celebration of Masses had been completed. He was buried in the Church of blessed Apollinaris. He occupied the see for 8 years, [lacuna] months, and [lacuna] days.

## SERGIUS, Archbishop XLI

[Col. 0786A]

Sergius XLI. Young in age, handsome in appearance. He had been a layman and had a bride, whom he took after assuming the governance of the Church. [Note: [Col. 0785D] This is false or exceedingly foolish. Sergius was married before governing the Church, and he assumed that office only after dismissing his wife. This is perfectly clear from Agnellus himself. ID.] During his time Pope Zacharias went to Francia, seeking assistance from the king of the Franks to expel the Lombards, because Aistulf, king of Italy, was oppressing Italy severely. This Sergius was an invader of the Church and was deposed by all the people of Ravenna. [Note: [Col. 0786D] By a later hand. ID.]

Others relate the following about Sergius:

“After these events had taken place, some time later Sergius, archbishop of Ravenna, departed this life; and immediately Michael, the record-keeper of that church, who held no priestly office, rose up and went to Ariminum to Mauritius. That utterly wicked Mauritius gathered an army and, together with the forces of Desiderius, king of the Lombards, hastened there. He entered Ravenna and, by force of arms, chose the aforementioned Michael and installed him in the episcopal residence of the Church of Ravenna. [Col. 0786B] He took Leo the archdeacon, who had been elected to the episcopal office, to Ariminum, and there the same Mauritius had him held in close confinement.”

[Note: [Col. 0786D] This final account is wrongly told of Leo of Ravenna. See Anastasius. ID.]

Thus the aforementioned Leo was later brought to the monastery of Saint Agatha the martyr; there, after three days, he ended his life because of the gouging out of his eyes.

## LEO, Archbishop XLII

Leo XLII. He was from this flock and not very tall in stature. He was buried in [lacuna] [lacuna] [lacuna].

## JOHN, Archbishop XLIII

John, [Note: [Col. 0786D] By a later hand. ID.] the sixth, XLIII. He was buried in the *ardica* of blessed Apollinaris. He occupied the see for 7 years, 1 month, and 3 days.

## GRATIOSUS, Archbishop XLIV

[Col. 0786C]

Gratiosus XLIV. A humble and gentle Israelite. In his time Charles, king of the Franks, came to Ravenna, invited by him to dinner, and dined with him. This man [Note: [Col. 0786D] By a later hand. ID.] prophesied, around the year of the Lord 810 [810], about events that were to occur in the city of Ravenna. He died on 23 February. He was buried in the church of blessed Apollinaris. He occupied the see for 3 years and 11 days.

## JOHN XLV

John, [Note: [Col. 0786D] Unknown to Agnellus. ID.] the seventh, XLV.

## VALERIUS, Archbishop XLVI

Valerius XLVI. On the fourth day before the Kalends of February, a feast is celebrated in the city of Classis.

## MARTIN, Archbishop XLVII

Martinus XLVII. He was tall and had a large [Col. 0786D] head. Pipin, king of the Lombards, died. In his time Pope Stephen also came to Ravenna, celebrated Mass in the Ursian church, and displayed the sandals of the Savior, which the entire people saw.

## PETRONACIUS, Archbishop XLVIII

Petronacius XLVIII. He swore allegiance to the honor of the emperor Charles. [Col. 0787A] In his time Andreas, also called Agnellus, abbot of Saint Mary at Blachernae and of Saint Bartholomew, flourished. He composed the *Book of Pontiffs* [Note: [Col. 0787D] By a later hand. BACCH.] (he was a cardinal priest of the Church of Ravenna). Also in his time the body of the most blessed Maximian, archbishop of the Church of Ravenna, was discovered.

## GEORGIUS, Archbishop XLIX

Georgius XLIX. He broke open all the public ecclesiastical treasuries, burst open the crypts, and extracted the treasures of his predecessors. And in order to raise Lothar’s daughter from the baptismal font, he spent great wealth on that occasion. In his time, at midday, the sun became exceedingly dark throughout the whole world until the ninth hour. He died on 24 January.

## DEODATUS, Archbishop L

[Col. 0787B]

Deusdedit, the fiftieth.

## JOHN, Archbishop LI

John VIII. He had the body of Saint Apollinaris carried to the church of Saint Martin in the Golden Heaven, out of fear of the Agarenes, who had carried away the silver *ciborium* from the church of Classis.

# ACTS OF THE ROMAN COUNCIL

[Col. 0787]

## NOTICE

[Col. 0787]

Since I obtained the acts of this council from the distinguished archive of the cathedral of Modena, and since they are scarcely even mentioned in the published collections of councils, I thought that they could appropriately be published here. This copy is a specimen, or summary, of what was done at that council for the protection of the bishops subject to the metropolitan Church of Ravenna [Col. 0787C] against John, bishop of Ravenna. Several copies of this document, made according to the council’s prescription, can be seen here; each was sent to a different bishop, so that the memory of the decrees might be transmitted to posterity. When compared with the published texts, these documents will shed much light on the ecclesiastical discipline of those times. They are as follows.

In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. In the fourth year of the pontificate of Our Lord Nicholas, supreme pontiff and universal pope; in the eleventh year of the empire of the most pious Augustus Louis; on the eighteenth day of the month of November, indiction 10. The chapters established and canonically confirmed in the holy council gathered at Rome by the most blessed Lord Pope Nicholas against John, archbishop of Ravenna.

**Chapter one.** You shall not consecrate bishops throughout Emilia except after the election of the clergy and people.

**Chapter two.** Whenever those same bishops wish to come to the Apostolic See, you shall in no way prohibit them. Nor shall you exact from them any payment contrary to canonical authority.

**Chapter three.** The estates which, after breaking the written grants, you transferred from the right of Saint Peter to the right of Saint Apollinaris, and which you distributed to individual persons by emphyteusis or by *libellus*, you must diligently investigate. When these persons have been found, cancel the emphyteusis or *libellus* and restore the estates to the rights of Saint Peter, to whom they belonged; and never again presume to do such a thing.

Bearing the concern of all the Churches of God, it is fitting that we provide for the needs of all and apply healing remedies to every wound; for we are shepherds of the Lord’s sheep. Yet the present care that falls especially upon us is all the greater in proportion as we represent the one to whom those sheep are specially entrusted by divine utterance, and to whom he also says by way of command: “And you, once converted, strengthen your brethren.” Therefore your holiness—namely, you bishops residing in Emilia—complains that you have been harassed by John, archbishop of Ravenna, through many acts of oppression. We must extend the hand of our apostolate to you as quickly as possible; and since you are among those brethren whom Saint Peter was converted to strengthen, it is necessary that, rescuing your fraternity from so many acts of oppression, we establish you upon the rock which he himself confessed, so that you may no longer [lacuna] [lacuna] [lacuna].

[Col. 0788B] It is established that your holiness, together with your brethren and fellow bishops of the region of Emilia, presented lamentable complaints in a mournful voice before the synod which we celebrated at Rome. It is known that John himself, archbishop of Ravenna, was present with a numerous gathering of most holy bishops, namely from Campania, Tuscany, the Pentapolis, and other regions. The first oppression and injury of which you complained that you had been afflicted by the aforesaid archbishop was, as you stated, that the same John, archbishop of Ravenna, went around your episcopal sees once every two years and remained in each one for as long as the very poverty—which is set aside here and there for the benefit of the episcopal office, the support of the clergy and poor, the administration of households, the reception of pilgrims, and the restoration of basilicas or episcopal residences—was consumed by him and his men; and that he did not depart before the bishop of that place had given to the archbishop and his household substantial gifts which were not owed.

Moreover, every year, in a manner found nowhere else in the world, you were compelled, as though paying tribute, to give sheep, *oblatae*, wine, chickens, and eggs to the archbishop, and similarly to his archpriest, archdeacon, *vicedominus*, treasurer, chamberlain, notary, record-keeper, defenders, chamberlain, and steward—three [units] for all those named above—an annual payment without interruption to each of those mentioned, as tributaries do.

You also asserted that he alienated and subjected to himself your parishes, titular churches, estates, and monasteries belonging to your episcopal office and entrusted to your administration, and destroyed them. You further stated, with no less complaint, that he compelled you to abandon your episcopal sees and, following the custom of the people, to serve at Ravenna each month in alternating or changing shifts, while the infants of your parishes died without chrism on those days. You also maintained that he was accustomed, at his own pleasure, to remove from your jurisdiction and discipline any clerics whom he newly judged to be of some usefulness.

With no less a great outcry you affirmed that the same archbishop did not allow you, whenever you wished to go to embrace the thresholds of the Apostles [Col. 0789A] or to come to the Apostolic See, to do so. When the most reverend bishops who were sitting in that same holy council heard these complaints and unheard-of assertions, they all cried out together that these things were being done contrary to the canons, and they humbly asked us to prohibit them forever by our episcopal authority.

Therefore, since such pernicious burdens and such an evil custom had tyrannically arisen in the Church of God, and since we were especially grieved that, contrary to all the rules of the holy Fathers and contrary to the entire custom of the Churches of God, such things had been rashly usurped by presumptuous men in the metropolitan Church of Ravenna alone, lest an opportunity remain for other metropolitan bishops to presume such acts, and lest the Church of God be corrupted by such an example, we have decreed together with the entire holy council that this be entirely removed from you and your successors, indeed from your holy Churches.

Accordingly, before the same reverend council, we prohibited John himself, archbishop, and all his successors; and, by apostolic authority, after pronouncing judgment on each presumption and promulgating the relevant sentences, we command that neither he nor his successors ever again presume to do anything of this kind. We have retained these chapters with us and ordered that copies of them be sent to you for preservation in future times.

But since your fraternity earnestly requested, for the future protection and complete security of your rights, that a precept of our authority be sent perpetually to you and to your successors in the episcopate, yielding to your prayers, through the text of this precept [Col. 0789C] we expressly command, order, and prohibit under every form of interdiction that no archbishop of Ravenna from now on and thereafter presume to approach your episcopal sees without your consent, to exact any money from you, or by any device to seize any property of your Church, your monasteries, your parishes, your titular churches, or your estates. Nor shall he presume in any way to summon you to Ravenna except at the times established by the Fathers, who decreed that councils of bishops be held twice a year.

This is especially to be suppressed: what they call the *trigesimale*—under no circumstances may they compel you to perform it at Ravenna, or presume to require you to do so. Thus it shall not be lawful for the archbishops of Ravenna to demand from you or from your successors in the episcopate any payment whatsoever, now or henceforth, that is, forever.

We also grant you permission, whenever you wish to hasten to Rome, out of love for the blessed Apostles or to visit the Apostolic See according to the custom of your predecessors, that the archbishop of Ravenna may presume to place no impediment in your way, openly or secretly; with God as your companion, you shall be permitted to go.

We further decree and define that when, at the established times, the archbishop of Ravenna summons you to councils, he shall in no way have permission to retain you longer, so that you shall not remain at Ravenna for more than fifteen days, except in a grave emergency.

According to the most salutary decree of Pope Saint Leo, he shall not have permission to remove from your discipline and subjection, without your consent, clerics of your mother church or diocese. Nor shall it be permitted to him to remove from your governance, authority, and ordination churches, parishes, titular churches, or monasteries belonging to your episcopal office.

Accordingly, we decree that both your clerics and all the property of your Church shall remain with you and your successors in the episcopate, with the freedom to govern, enjoy, and administer them. We do not wish the archbishop of Ravenna to have any power or authority over you beyond what the sacred canons prescribe.

If at any time any archbishop of Ravenna should attempt to renew or restore the aforesaid burdens against you, or, after a long period, try to assert that you had paid them and endeavor to prove that the archbishop of Ravenna had possessed such a right over you in ancient times, no such assertion shall have force, nor shall the length of time be able to support it, since it is clear that the practice had long been presumptuously maintained contrary to the rule of justice. This is especially so because the sacred canons teach that an evil custom must be avoided no less than a pernicious corruption.

Therefore we decree that you shall provide nothing to the archbishop of Ravenna who holds office at any given time except what the holy canons prescribe and what the other bishops throughout Liguria, Venetia, and Istria are known to provide to their metropolitans. We judge that the archbishop of Ravenna ought to exact nothing from you, and we define that he may exercise no right over you except as stated above.

If from now on and thereafter any archbishop of Ravenna attempts to act contrary to the command of our apostolic authority or contrary, in whole or in part, to the tenor of this decree; if he imposes upon you or your successors in the episcopate anything prohibited above, or lays any of the aforementioned burdens upon you, and does not obey in every respect the text of this document, let him be bound by the sentence of Almighty God and of the blessed Apostles Peter and Paul, the chief Apostles, and by the authority of the Apostolic See with the bonds of anathema; and, as a contumacious violator of the sacred canons and apostolic institutions, let him be forever excluded from every priestly office.

We confirm and strengthen forever the matters written above, saving only the honor and subjection owed to the holy Roman Church, together with teachable reverence and fitting obedience to the bishops of the Apostolic See.

Under the terms of this precept, written by the hand of Leo the record-keeper, he subscribed in indiction 10.

The names of the bishops who were present at this holy council, consented, and subscribed are as follows:

Hdebrandus of Veroli. John of Velletri. Peter of Gabi. Magistus of Porto. Arsenius of Orte. Petronacius of Albano. Liutprand of Chiusi. [Col. 0791A] Peter of Arezzo. Geremias of Sabina. Ragio of Narni. Ropertus of Nocera. Arigisus of Foligno. John of Forconium. Leodrosius of Marsica. Colo of Rieti. Arnulf of Belluno. Osipus of Pistoia. Anselm of Camerino. Lanstriensis of Pesaro. ## [CONSTITUTION OF SACRED LAW]

### NOTICE TO THE FOLLOWING CONSTITUTION

[Col. 0793]

This famous Gerbert was first archbishop of Rheims, having previously been a monk of Fleury; afterward he was archbishop of Ravenna and then Roman pontiff under the name Sylvester II. Much has been written about him. I am pleased to present here, from the highly esteemed Farfa manuscript, the constitution of Otto III against those who alienate the property of Churches, which from its inscription I readily believe to have been dictated by Gerbert.

A notable point in the same inscription is that a synod was held at Rome in the year there given, 998, in the month of September, and that Arnulf, archbishop of Milan, was dealt with there. I do not remember having read anything about this elsewhere. It should also be noted that the author of this Chronicle, who wrote Herbert for Gerbert, later attributes to Gibert a story assigned to Gerbert.

The inscription and constitution mentioned above are as follows.

### [CONSTITUTION]

Here begins the constitution of the sacred law of the lord Emperor Otto, issued on the twelfth day before the Kalends of October, indiction 12, in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Gregory V; promulgated by the hand of Gerbert, archbishop of the holy Church of Ravenna, at the synod in which Arnulf, bishop of Milan, was deprived of the papacy in the basilica of blessed Peter called at the Golden Cell, and all the bishops who were present subscribed.

Otto, by the grace of God emperor of the Romans, Augustus and consul of the Senate and People of Rome, to the archbishops, abbots, margraves, counts, and all judges established in Italy, forever.

We have learned that bishops and abbots abuse the possessions of the Churches and assign them by written instruments to various persons, not for the benefit of the Churches but for the sake of money, kinship, and friendship. When their successors are admonished to restore the houses of God, fulfill the duties of the commonwealth, and render service to us, they complain that the estates of their Churches are held by others and plainly demonstrate that they cannot carry out what has been commanded.

Therefore, because the condition of the Churches of God is being destroyed, and because our imperial majesty also suffers no small loss when those subject to us cannot render the services owed to us, we establish and confirm by imperial edict that no written instrument—whether issued under the name of a *libellus*, by emphyteusis, or by any other means—concerning anything belonging to the Churches of God shall be valid.

When the grantor dies, let the instrument die with him; let the loss fall solely upon the person who bound and obligated himself by that document, and let none of the damages arising from the superscription belong to the person who succeeded him in the administration. Rather, let the successor have complete freedom to recall to the ownership of the Church everything that has been alienated through *libelli* or any other written instrument, and to arrange matters so that he may render the service owed to God and to us.

For since kings and emperors are not permitted to give away what belongs to a kingdom or empire except during their lifetime, with the exception of Churches, how should abbots and bishops be permitted to distribute the property of Churches throughout the periods of their successors?

Every right, whether law, written instrument, or custom of any kind, if it is contrary to the benefit of the Church, must be annulled; nor should those measures be confirmed by our authority which are proved to have been introduced against the author and propagator of the empire.

Let this one written instrument therefore be held as law in such matters: the one that benefits the Church of God and cannot in any way harm it.

If anyone should attempt to act against this constitution of ours, let him be judged a rebel, and let him be anathema, *maranatha*, unless he repents, by all the bishops who subscribed to this edict of our empire, or who gave or will give their assent. Amen.

The Chronicle follows.

[Col. 0794]
